Inherited from Old Galician-Portuguese real, from Latin rēgālis (“royal”), from rēx (“king”) + -ālis, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃rḗǵs (“ruler, king”). Equivalent to rei + -al.
* (currency used in Brazil since 1994): from Unidade Real de Valor (“Real Unit of Value”), an intermediary unit pegged to the US dollar which was introduced during a transitional period from the cruzeiro-real as a measure to combat inflation. Although the word real is clearly used to invoke the meaning of “actual value” (hence the plural reais), a connection to the former currency real (etymology 1, plural réis) is likely also intentional. As such, most dictionaries inform Latin rēgālis as the word’s etymon.
raw_glosses: (historical, plural reais) real (former unit of currency used in Spain and its colonies)
